elements.element: If renewal is not automatic, renewal may occur only by mutual written agreement.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent because the clause expressly selects automatic renewal: “will automatically renew.”

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause provides for automatic renewal for “additional 1-year terms.”

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on 30 days’ written notice.
elements.evidence: Customer may terminate for any reason after the Initial Term on 30 days’ written notice. This continuing termination right is at least as protective as a 30-day opt-out from a renewal term, although it is not drafted as an express non-renewal right.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must provide Customer a reminder 60 days before each renewal.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires Kubient to send a renewal reminder.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no price-increase cap or CPI limitation.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer’s required non-renewal notice may not exceed 60 days.
elements.evidence: Customer has a 30-day written-notice termination right following the Initial Term, which is shorter than the permitted 60-day maximum and allows Customer to exit renewing terms.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: No operative language limits renewal price increases to 5%.

result.reason: The redline supplies automatic one-year renewals and a Customer 30-day exit right, satisfying the notice component of both positions. It omits the mandatory Vendor reminder and every required price-increase cap, so neither level is complete. It is also not minimal: beyond reducing Customer’s notice period, it changes Kubient’s convenience-termination right by making termination effective only at the end of the then-current Term. The remaining termination-for-cause, insolvency, and fee provisions remain operative without an internal contradiction.
